newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks choppy after opening steady.
newsitem.headline: French stocks choppy after opening steady.

text.p: French shares were little changed on Monday and traders said while the market should be supported by buying on the first account day it was still under the sway of softer domestic and German bonds, a retracing of the dollar and New York's mixed close last Friday.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index was up 3.80 points or 0.15 percent at 2,566.64 at 0921 GMT while the CAC-40 futures contract was down eight at 2,569 from Friday's close.

Club Mediterranee busy, surges 16.85 percent to 415.4 francs, after being suspended limit up twice in morning. Shares in the resorts company were suspended on Friday when it announced annual net losses of 743 million francs, after restructuring charges.

Saint-Louis active, rises 1.66 percent to 1,530 on Friday's merger news with Worms et Cie down 4.12 percent to 396. The merger terms represent a five percent premium based on Monday's prices and 10 percent on Friday.
Dassault Systemes roars up 8.26 percent to 354 francs, brokers not immmediately sure why.

Axa gains in line with the market, up 0.49 percent to 372.8. Axa declined comment on a British newspaper article which reported it was looking to auction off its Equity & Law subsidiary, which could fetch as much as one billion stg.

Eramet drops almost 10 percent to 276 francs after the French government said it would expropriate the mining rights of its Koniambo field held by subsidiary, Le Nickel. Eramet said it would fight the decision, which would cause "considerable prejudice".
CLF-Dexia gains 4.33 percent to 530, on news it would announce an "important financial operation" later today.
